data.title: As France's problems multiply, so do its presidential hopefuls
data.description:
Key points:
  • Judo champion, ex-PM, Riviera mayor shake up France's 2027 race
  • Proliferation of candidates highlights decline of traditional party machines
  • Le Pen, Melenchon remain clear frontrunners despite crowded field

By Michel Rose

A judo champion, a Riviera mayor and a former French prime minister are the latest pretenders to the Elysee, but despite injecting some intrigue into the presidential election none of them have dislodged far-right leader Marine Le Pen and hard-left veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon from the top of the polls.

In the past few weeks five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner declared his intention to run, former Prime Minister Dominique de Villepin launched a long-anticipated campaign, and David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes, has surged in opinion polls, overtaking former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe in some surveys.

President Emmanuel Macron's insurgent victory nearly a decade ago shattered the traditional party system, but his rise has hollowed out the political centre and encouraged a growing cast of hopefuls. There are more than 30 declared or prospective candidates.

"Governing parties have weakened and candidates increasingly emerge from the media spotlight," Socialist lawmaker Romain Eskenazi told Reuters. "People say: 'Why not me?'"

For now, polls suggest the crowded field may be helping rather than hurting the two frontrunners by leaving them without a credible mainstream rival who can marshal support from moderate, centre-right and mainstream-left voters.

With France rocked by protests and politicians struggling to tame a bulging deficit, many voters appear unimpressed by the presidential offering.

In a November 12 Odoxa poll for Le Figaro, more than three-quarters of respondents said the high number of candidates showed that "many people have overinflated egos".

RIGHTWINGER LISNARD SURGES, OTHERS WAIT IN WINGS

Lisnard is the best performer so far after Le Pen and Melenchon. The free-market conservative scored 11% in a recent RTL-Toluna poll, ahead of Philippe on 9%, pushing Macron's former prime minister into fifth place behind centre-left candidate Raphael Glucksmann.

Lisnard argues that France's establishment has failed to tackle debt, crime and red tape. He has echoed Argentine President Javier Milei by filming himself shredding regulations.

Long regarded as the strongest contender from France's pro-business centre, Philippe has been the main loser from Lisnard's rise, with some saying his campaign lacks momentum and clear ideas.

But others dismiss Lisnard's rise as temporary.

"I think it's a bubble," Pieyre-Alexandre Anglade, a lawmaker from Macron's party, told Reuters.

At the annual mayors' gathering in Paris, where candidates seek endorsements to make the ballot, many officials remained undecided. Eric Berlivet, mayor of Roche-la-Moliere near Lyon, said he admired both Lisnard and Philippe, and would pick his candidate in January.

"We've been disappointed too often by national leaders," he said. "I want someone who makes everyday life easier."

There has been talk of a primary between the centrist and rightwing candidates, but the politicians have so far not agreed on a process.

"Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Melenchon may be leading the polls, but our responsibility is to unite the centre and the right, not launch a primary that would sow confusion and deepen divisions," Jeremie Patrier-Leitus, a spokesperson for Philippe's campaign, told Reuters.

Despite having no political experience, Riner polls around 4%, outperforming several established party leaders such as Greens leader Marine Tondelier and Communist veteran Fabien Roussel. De Villepin, who has won support for his pro-Palestinian views, polls around 3%.

Riner presents himself as an outsider with fresh ideas. Asked at the mayors' conference whether he was entering the race because politicians were not up to the job, he said: "I wouldn't have necessarily phrased it like that, but yes."

There has also been speculation about a possible late run by European Central Bank chief Christine Lagarde, who will step down in February — two months before the April first-round vote. She scored as much as 14% in a recent poll for Politico, but she has remained mum about her intentions.

Former Socialist President Francois Hollande has said he is also mulling putting his name forward.

LE PEN AND MELENCHON UNAFFECTED SO FAR

Christian Le Bart, a political scientist at Sciences Po Rennes, said, "Being outside the main political parties has become an asset."

But it also has its limits.

Riner has appeared to struggle on some policy questions and challenged mainstream thinking by saying "Ukraine was not our war". Meanwhile, de Villepin's failed 2012 presidential campaign showed how hard it can be to secure the 500 signatures from elected officials needed to make the ballot.

While the centre and traditional parties of left and right splinter into competing candidacies, Le Pen and Melenchon continue to dominate. Le Pen remains the candidate to beat, leading most first-round polls and runoff scenarios. A Paris appeals court in July upheld an embezzlement conviction for Le Pen but set the terms of her ban from public office in a way that still allows her to run, though she has appealed to the Court of Cassation, France's highest court.

"She is seen as winning in almost all the second-round scenarios," Le Bart said, adding that her decade-long normalisation strategy had changed her National Rally party's image.

However, he warned against concluding it was a done deal, as the field will inevitably narrow as the vote nears, injecting unpredictability.

"The race is far from over," he said.

data.title: HDFC Bank shares tread water as rally loses steam
data.description:
HDFC Bank shares were nearly flat on Friday, edging up just 0.10 per cent to ₹862.85 on the NSE, as the week's strong momentum faded and volumes dropped sharply, pointing to a consolidation phase after a near-30 per cent rebound from October lows.

The stock opened at ₹857.90, touched a high of ₹866.25, and saw no fresh leg higher. Traded value fell to ₹1,472.53 crore on volume of 170.76 lakh shares, roughly half Thursday's traded value, with sellers accounting for 68 per cent of total traded quantity. Delivery-based trades stood at 69 per cent, suggesting the remaining activity was largely short-term in nature.

There were no exchange filings from the bank on Friday. This week's key corporate development was Wednesday's board approval of Dr Harsh Kumar Bhanwala's re-appointment as Independent Director for a fresh five-year term from January 2027, subject to shareholder approval.

The NSE flagged that HDFC Bank's close-to-close price movement exceeded 25 per cent in the prior month, a standard surveillance indicator triggered by the stock's sharp recovery from its 52-week low of ₹669.20 on October 28.

HDFC Bank's year-to-date loss stood at 13.01 per cent, against the Nifty 50's 1.68 per cent decline. The stock trades at a P/E of 16.61 and remains roughly 15 per cent below its 52-week high of ₹1,017.50.

Bank Nifty consolidated near 63,535, with analysts watching the 64,000 mark as the next decisive trigger.

data.description:
RNS Number : 8907E Tooru PLC 27 November 2026  

27 November 2026

Tooru plc

(“Tooru” or the “Company”)

New funding facility and related party transaction

Tooru, the AIM listed company focused on the branded health and wellness sector, is pleased to announce that it has entered into a funding facility (the “Facility”) with S-Ventures plc (“SVEN”) to provide the Company with additional funding for continued investment into the Company’s principal operating businesses and for the Company’s ’s working capital requirements.

The Facility

The Facility is a two-year unsecured facility for up to £500,000 and is expected to be drawn down in tranches of £100,000.  Each drawdown will require approval of the Board of SVEN and will be subject to prevailing market conditions at the time of any drawdown request.  Annual interest of 5% will accrue on each drawdown and principal and interest for each drawdown will be repayable on the second anniversary of each drawdown date.

Additionally, on each drawdown, Tooru will issue to SVEN two separate tranches of warrants over the Company’s ordinary shares. The number of warrants to be issued in the first tranche (the “First Tranche Warrants”) will be calculated by dividing the amount drawn down (the “Drawdown Amount”) by the Company’s closing share price on the trading day immediately prior to the issue of a drawdown notice (the “Reference Price”) and multiplied by 1.5. The First Tranche Warrants will have an exercise price equal to the Reference Price. The number of warrants to be issued in the second tranche of warrants (the “Second Tranche Warrants” and together with the First Tranche Warrants, the “Warrants”) will be calculated by dividing the Drawdown Amount by the Reference Price increased by a premium of 78 per cent. (the "Second Tranche Exercise Price"). The exercise price of the Second Tranche Warrants will be equal to the Second Tranche Exercise Price. The life of both Warrants will be 3 years from their date of issue.

Related party transaction

By virtue of its significant shareholding of 14.91% in the Company and commonality of a director, Scott Livingston, SVEN is a related party as defined in the AIM Rules.  Accordingly, the entering into the Facility is considered to be a Related Party Transaction ("Transaction") pursuant to Rule 13 of the AIM Rules. Mr Livingston has been recused from the formal consideration of the Transaction by the Board.

The Directors of the Company who are independent of the Transaction, having consulted with the Company's Nominated Adviser, Beaumont Cornish, consider the terms of the Transaction to be fair and reasonable insofar as the Company's shareholders are concerned.

Scott Livingston, CEO of Tooru plc, commented:

“The Company continues to demonstrate strong momentum in building its various businesses.  This funding facility will provide additional funds for further investment into the Company’s key businesses and for general working capital purposes.”

data.description:
RNS Number : 8841E M. P. Evans Group PLC 27 November 2026  

M.P. EVANS GROUP PLC

(“M.P. Evans”, “the Group”, or “the Company”)

STRONG CROP AND PRODUCTION GROWTH AND FURTHER £2 MILLION SHARE BUYBACK ALLOCATION

M.P. Evans Group PLC, a producer of sustainable Indonesian palm oil, is pleased to announce continued strong crop and production growth during the second half of 2026, and that the Group is allocating a further £2 million to its existing share-buyback programme.

In the 2026 interim results announcement on 14 September 2026, the Group reported that the total crop harvested during the first half of the year from the areas managed by it (including own hectarage plus that managed on behalf of associated scheme smallholders) was 705,400 tonnes, up by 14% from the same period in the previous year. This strong performance has continued through to the end of October with the equivalent figure for the ten-month year-to-date increase remaining at 14%. Despite an extended period of dry weather in several of the Group’s properties in the middle part of the year, Group estates have performed well, and the board anticipates that recent rainfall will continue to support cropping levels during the last quarter.

Again, consistent with the position at the half-year, total crop processed for the ten months to October 2026 is up by 8% as the Group continues to restrict the amount of lower margin outside crop brought in for processing. However, pleasingly, total crude palm oil (“CPO”) output is now up by 13% on the same point last year, as oil-extraction rates have continued to improve during the second half of the year. This increase in production has also helped to further reduce unit costs from the amounts reported in the interim results. The Group is working hard to ensure that production is despatched on a timely basis, but there may be a small amount of carryover into 2027 which will be of benefit to that year’s results.

Pricing for the Group’s output has, thus far, remained at similar levels in the second half of 2026 with the year-to-date ex-mill-gate price for the Group’s CPO at US$866 per tonne for the ten months to October, only 1% different to the US$873 reported at June. There may be some slight price softening towards the end of the year, with supply increasing and good stocks available, notably in Malaysia, but we anticipate some price recovery in early 2027.

Indonesia has experienced the effect of the El Nino weather phenomenon during 2026, and this may lead to a small reduction in total national palm oil output in 2027. By contrast, production from Group estates is expected to remain robust, benefiting from a combination of geographic diversity, natural yield increases as several young areas continue to mature, and management’s continuing commitment to high agronomic standards across the Group’s estate portfolio.

The Group announced on 5 October 2026 that it was extending its share buyback programme with a budget of £3 million, and set out in that announcement the basis upon which the programme was being implemented. Given the ongoing strength of the Group’s performance, the board has decided to allocate a further £2 million to the programme (on the same basis as disclosed in the 5 October 2026 announcement) with immediate effect.

The Group will provide a further trading update for the whole of 2026 in its crop, pricing and production announcement due to be released in January 2027.

M.P. Evans Group PLC chief executive Matthew Coulson commented on the Group’s performance:

“As we move into the closing stages of 2026, the Group has continued to perform well, both operationally and financially, and the board is confident that the Group will deliver some excellent results for the year as a whole.”

data.title: REG - Jadestone Energy PLC - Publication of Circular and Notice of Meeting
data.description:
RNS Number : 9773E Jadestone Energy PLC 27 November 2026  

Publication of Circular and Notice of Requisitioned General Meeting

Board unanimously recommends that shareholders vote AGAINST all the Resolutions to stop Prima Energy gaining control of Jadestone without paying a control premium

27 November 2026 – Singapore: Jadestone Energy plc (AIM:JSE) (the “Company” and together with its subsidiaries, “Jadestone”), an independent upstream production and development company focused on the Asia-Pacific region, announces that, following the requisition notice received on 20 November 2026 on behalf of PT Prima Petroleum Energi (“Prima Energy”), it has today published a circular to shareholders (the “Circular”) containing notice of a general meeting of the Company (the “Requisitioned General Meeting”) to be held at 1.00 p.m. (GMT) on Monday, 21 December 2026 at the offices of K&L Gates LLP, 5th Floor, One New Change, London EC4M 9AF.

At the Requisitioned General Meeting, shareholders will be asked to consider two ordinary resolutions, proposed by Prima Energy, to appoint Pieters Adyana Utomo, Chief Executive Officer of Prima Energy and Alexander Paul Blakeley OBE, former President and CEO of Jadestone Energy, as directors of the Company (the “Resolutions”). The Circular also contains a statement by Prima Energy, which the Company is required to circulate under section 314 of the Companies Act 2006.

The Circular, which includes the Notice of Requisitioned General Meeting, has been published on the Company’s website at www.jadestone-energy.com and is being posted to shareholders today, together with a Form of Proxy.

JADESTONE’S BOARD OF DIRECTORS UNANIMOUSLY RECOMMENDS THAT SHAREHOLDERS VOTE AGAINST ALL THE PRIMA ENERGY RESOLUTIONS.

Dr. Adel Chaouch, Executive Chairman of Jadestone Energy, commented:

“The fiduciary duty of Jadestone’s Board of Directors is to protect and create value for all shareholders.  Prima Energy is clearly a competitor of Jadestone and, in the Board’s view, is displaying a clear intent to opportunistically take control of the Company. The Board urges shareholders to vote and unanimously recommends that shareholders vote AGAINST all the Resolutions to stop Prima Energy from taking control of your company without paying an appropriate premium for all shareholders and using proprietary information for its own purposes to the detriment of shareholders.”

It is clear to the Board that Prima Energy’s ultimate goal is to gain control of the Company without paying an appropriate premium to its shareholders. The Board considers that Prima Energy’s arguments in support of the Resolutions are self-serving and an attempt to secure Board representation and access to proprietary information without an appropriate relationship agreement in place that protects the rights of all shareholders. The Board believes that this would be detrimental to all other Jadestone shareholders and potentially lead to a destruction of shareholder value.

The Board set out the background to the requisition in its announcement of 23 November 2026. The letter from the Chairman in the Circular sets out the Board’s full reasons for its recommendation, including the following:

  • On 2 September 2026, Prima Energy announced that it had agreed to acquire approximately 28.3 per cent. of the Company’s issued share capital from funds managed by Tyrus Capital S.A.M. (“Tyrus Capital”) and stated that it had no intention of making an offer for the Company, a statement by which it is bound under Rule 2.8 of the Takeover Code. The Board understands that Prima Energy paid a very substantial premium to the average share price over the month prior to the acquisition, with Prima Energy repeatedly refusing to disclose the price it paid.
  • On 7 September 2026, Prima Energy proposed to the Company what was effectively a deed of control. Among other things, it:
    • would have entitled Prima Energy to nominate two directors while holding 20 per cent. or more, whom the Company would have been obliged to appoint without any assessment by the Board or its Nominated Adviser;
    • would have entitled Prima Energy to place each of its directors on every Board committee; and to receive, each quarter, monthly production by field, operating cost per barrel, realised prices and capital expenditure; and
    • contained no standstill, which is a key protection for other shareholders against Prima Energy having a route to control without paying shareholders a premium for it.
  • Although the draft deed of control was subsequently withdrawn, the Board believes that Prima Energy’s underlying aim remains unchanged.
  • At the same time as proposing the deed of control, Prima Energy proposed that the Company's Chairman should step down from the Board, with Mr Utomo and Mr Blakeley to join the Board, as part of Prima Energy's proposed “leadership transition”.
  • On 28 October 2026, the Company offered Prima Energy the right to nominate one director, subject to a relationship agreement based on the agreement formerly in place with Tyrus Capital, with the addition of further protections reflecting Prima Energy’s position as a direct competitor and the manner of acquisition of its shares (no price having been disclosed) and the previous interactions on the deed of control. Prima Energy rejected this offer. Since 28 October 2026, designated members of the Board have had various interactions with Mr Utomo and Prima Energy on the content of an appropriate relationship agreement.
  • Prima Energy is a direct competitor of the Company in its core operating areas and has refused to enter into a relationship agreement that the Board considers would protect the rights of all shareholders. Prima Energy has also repeatedly asked to appoint a director to the Board with no relationship agreement in place at all, which the Board considers a disregard for basic governance norms and evidence of a desire to access Company information without restraint. Neither of the proposed directors can be considered independent. Mr Utomo is also President Director of PT Soechi Lines Tbk, a vessel owner and operator, and the Company’s potential service providers may be reluctant to bid for its contracts if the head of a competing service provider sits on its Board.
  • The Board does not consider that the return of Mr Blakeley, a former executive of the Company and the nominee of a single shareholder, is consistent with the Company’s governance framework or the orderly leadership transition completed under the current Board. In early November 2026, Prima Energy met several of the Company’s shareholders in the UK. Although Mr Utomo had advised the Company that Prima Energy would not take the discussions about two Board seats to shareholders and that he had “disengaged” from Mr Blakeley, Mr Blakeley represented Prima Energy at all of those meetings, with Board composition, including the intention to seek two Board seats, a central topic.
  • The Board does not consider Prima Energy’s request comparable to the Board representation previously granted to significant shareholders. Tyrus Capital and Livermore Partners were effectively founder shareholders, were not competitors of the Company and provided early-stage capital to build the Company. Prima Energy is a new shareholder and a competitor seeking control without paying a control premium to shareholders.
  • The Company continues to target a final investment decision on its Vietnam gas development before the end of 2026. The Requisitioned General Meeting diverts the Company’s time and resources from that Vietnam gas development at a critical point.

Bradda Head Lithium Ltd

(“Bradda”, "BHL" or the "Company")

Completion of first year expenditure programme at Whistlejacket

Bradda Head Lithium Ltd (AIM: BHL), the North America-focused lithium development company, announces the successful completion of eight core holes totaling approximately 1,559.87 meters and a planned, temporary pause of core drilling at the Whistlejacket Lithium Project ("Whistlejacket" or "WJ"), held under the Company's Option to Joint Venture agreement with Kennecott Exploration Company ("KEX") to effect critical improvements to the drilling equipment.

Highlights:

  • Eight core holes totaling approximately 1,559.87 meters completed at Whistlejacket (WSTL0020 to WSTL0027 – Figure 1) since drilling commenced on August 21st, 2026;
  • First-year expenditure commitment was achieved under the Option to Joint Venture agreement with KEX (see PR dated January 27, 2026);
  • Results from step-out drill hole WSTL0020 were encouraging, with an intersection of 31.8m at 1.07% Li2O (see PR dated 13 Oct 2026)
  • Assay results for WSTL0022 returned a core length-weighted average grade of 1.34% Li₂O over 38.13m (64.01m to 102.14m downhole), including a higher-grade 23.39m interval grading 1.62% Li₂O from 64.01m (see PR dated 25 Nov 2026).
  • Pause enables the Company to review results and refine the next phase of drilling;
  • The pause coincides with the Christmas and New Year holiday period, avoiding a partly staffed, start-stop programme over the holidays;
  • Assay results for the remaining holes will be reported as they are received and verified; and
  • Drilling is expected to restart in Q1 2027.

Ian Stalker, Executive Chair, commented:

"The first phase of drilling at Whistlejacket has delivered what we set out to achieve. We have completed eight holes and around 1,559.87 meters, met our first-year expenditure commitment with KEX, and confirmed that spodumene mineralization continues to depth and along strike. Taking a short, planned break now is the sensible step. It gives our technical team time to incorporate the results into a sharper future drill plan. We expect to return to site early in 2027 and we look forward to reporting the remaining assay results in the meantime."

Drilling progress

Since the start of the 2026 campaign, the Company has completed eight diamond core holes at Whistlejacket for a total of approximately 1,559.87 meters (Figure 1). The programme was designed to test the continuity of the spodumene-bearing pegmatite intersected in KEX's previous drilling, both along strike and down-dip. Results reported to date from WSTL0020 (1.07% Li₂O over 31.8m) and assay results for WSTL0022 returned a core length-weighted average grade of 1.34% Li₂O over 38.13m (64.01m to 102.14m downhole), including a higher-grade 23.39m interval grading 1.62% Li₂O from 64.01m confirm that mineralization continues to depth and along strike (see PR dated 13 October 2026 and PR dated 25 Nov 2026).

Core from the remaining holes has been logged and sampled, and samples have been submitted to SGS for analysis. Assay results will be reported once received and reviewed under the Company's QAQC procedures.

Pause of core drilling

With the first-year expenditure commitment of US$750,000 under the Option to Joint Venture agreement with KEX now delivered (see PR dated January 27, 2026), the Company considers this an appropriate point to pause, review and plan. The pause will allow the Company to:

  • integrate the geological, structural and assay data from the first eight holes into an updated geological model, and use this to prioritize and optimize the next drill holes;
  • improve operational planning with the drilling contractor, including rig scheduling, drill pad and access preparation, and core handling logistics, to increase productivity when drilling resumes; and
  • allow the drilling contractor to implement essential maintenance and improvements to the rig, reducing the risk of downtime during the next phase and potentially reducing on-going costs.

Next steps

The Company expects to remobilize and restart drilling at Whistlejacket early 2027. During the pause, the technical team will continue core logging, sample tracking and interpretation work, and will finalize the drill plan for the next phase. The Company will provide further updates on assay results and on the restart of drilling in due course.

Glossary of Technical Terms

Term

Definition

AIM

The AIM market of the London Stock Exchange.

Airborne geophysics

Surveys flown by aircraft or drone that measure physical properties of the ground, such as magnetism or radiometrics, to help with geological mapping and targeting.

Along strike

In the direction of a geological unit’s strike, meaning the horizontal line where it meets the surface.

Assay

Laboratory analysis that measures the grade of a rock sample.

Brine

Saline groundwater that may contain dissolved lithium and other elements.

Claim

An unpatented mining claim on federal (BLM) land, which gives the holder the right to explore for and develop minerals.

Core drilling / diamond core hole

Drilling with a diamond-impregnated bit that recovers a solid cylinder of rock (core) for logging and assay.

Down-dip

In the direction a geological unit slopes downward from the surface.

Drill pad

A prepared, levelled area where a drill rig is set up.

Environmental Assessment (EA)

An analysis under the U.S. National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) of the likely environmental effects of a proposed action on federal land.

ha

Hectare (10,000 m², about 2.47 acres).

Indicated Mineral Resource

The part of a Mineral Resource whose quantity, grade, densities, shape and physical characteristics are estimated with enough confidence to support mine planning and evaluation of economic viability.

Inferred Mineral Resource

The part of a Mineral Resource whose quantity and grade are estimated from limited geological evidence and sampling. It has a lower level of confidence than an Indicated Mineral Resource.

kt / Mt

Thousand tonnes / million tonnes.

LCE

Lithium carbonate equivalent (Li₂CO₃). It is the industry measure of contained lithium (1 t Li = 5.323 t LCE).

Li

The chemical symbol for lithium.

Li₂O

Lithium oxide. Grades in hard-rock (pegmatite) deposits are usually expressed as % Li₂O (1% Li = 2.153% Li₂O).

Logging

Systematic recording of the geological features of drill core, such as rock type, mineralogy and structure.

m

Metres.

MAR

The Market Abuse Regulation (EU No. 596/2014) as it forms part of UK domestic law.

Measured Mineral Resource

The part of a Mineral Resource whose quantity, grade, densities, shape and physical characteristics are estimated with enough confidence to support detailed mine planning and final evaluation of economic viability.

Mineral Exploration Permit

A permit issued by the Arizona State Land Department (ASLD) that allows mineral exploration on State Trust land.

Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE)

An estimate of the tonnage and grade of mineralisation with reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction, prepared to a recognised reporting code.

Mineralisation

The concentration of economically significant minerals in a rock mass.

NI 43-101

Canadian National Instrument 43-101, Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

Nomad

Nominated Adviser, the corporate adviser that every AIM company must appoint under the AIM Rules.

Notice of Intent (NOI)

A notice filed with the BLM for exploration that disturbs 5 acres or less.

Option to Joint Venture

An agreement under which the Company can earn an interest in a project by meeting set expenditure and other commitments.

Pegmatite

A very coarse-grained igneous rock, usually granitic, that can host lithium minerals such as spodumene.

Plan of Operations

A BLM authorisation needed for exploration or mining that disturbs more than 5 acres.

ppm

Parts per million.

QAQC

Quality assurance and quality control. These procedures, such as inserting standards, blanks and duplicates, check the accuracy and precision of sampling and assay results.

Qualified Person (QP)

A person who meets the professional and experience requirements of NI 43-101 and the AIM Note for Mining and Oil & Gas Companies.

Regulatory Information Service (RIS)

A service approved by the London Stock Exchange to distribute regulatory announcements.

Remobilise

To return the drill rig, crew and equipment to site so drilling can restart.

SGS

SGS S.A., an independent, internationally accredited laboratory that provides analytical services.

Spodumene

A lithium aluminium silicate mineral (LiAlSi₂O₆) and the main commercial source of hard-rock lithium.

Step-out drill hole

A hole drilled some distance from known mineralisation to test whether it extends.

Ariana Resources plc (AIM: AAU, ASX: AA2, “Ariana” or the “Company”), advancing towards gold production at its 100%-owned 1.6Moz (pre-tax NPV10: US$1.056 billion*) Dokwe Gold Project in Zimbabwe, today announces that it will convene to hold a General Meeting of the shareholders at 11:00am on 15 December 2026 at the East India Club, 16 St James’s Square, London, SW1 4LH.

The Company has announced the General Meeting to seek Shareholder approval for the following Resolutions, of which Resolutions 1 to 11 will be proposed as ordinary resolutions and Resolution 12 as a special resolution:

1) Approval of the long-term incentive plan for the purposes of ASX Listing Rule 7.2, Exception 13

2) Grant of performance rights to Dr Kerim Sener for the purposes of ASX Listing Rule 10.14

3) Grant of options to Andrew du Toit for the purposes of ASX Listing Rule 10.14

4) Grant of performance rights to Michael Atkins for the purposes of ASX Listing Rule 10.14

5) Ratification of agreement to issue tranche 1 shares to Dendere

6) Ratification of agreement to issue tranche 2 shares to Dendere

7) Ratification of agreement to grant the call option to Dendere

8) Ratification of issue of placement shares

9) Approval to issue Xinhai tranche 3 CDIs and Xinhai tranche 3 CDI options pursuant to the Xinhai investment agreement

10) Approval to issue Hongmen CDIs and Hongmen CDI options to Hongmen pursuant to tranche 3 of the investment

11) Approval for headroom capacity to issue and allot shares

12) Approval of headroom capacity to issue and allot shares on a non-pre-emptive basis

Reasons for the General Meeting

The General Meeting has been convened primarily to comply with various ASX Listing Rules requirements.

In addition, whilst the various issues of Ordinary Shares referred to in Resolutions 5 to 10 may be made in accordance with the authorities obtained at the Annual General Meeting held on 29 May 2026, the Company is also taking the opportunity to seek additional authorities to issue Ordinary Shares to provide future flexibility should opportunities arise.

  • ADOPTION OF THE LTIP AND GRANT OF AWARDS (RESOLUTIONS 1 TO 4)

The reason for adoption of the LTIP is to attract, motivate and retain key employees, contractors and other persons who provide services to the Company, and the Company considers that the adoption of the LTIP and the future grant of awards under the LTIP will provide these parties with the opportunity to participate in the future growth of the Company, whilst also aligning their remuneration with performance conditions (including share price targets and Dokwe Project milestones) which are expected to add value for Shareholders.

A summary of the principal terms of the LTIP which provides for performance rights and options to be issued in respect of up to 100 million new Ordinary Shares is set out in Annexure A of the Circular, the terms of the awards proposed to be granted to Dr Kerim Sener, Andrew du Toit and Michael Atkins under Resolutions 2 to 4 are described in the Explanatory Statement in the Circular and the valuations provided in accordance with the ASX Rules in respect of those proposed grants are set out in Annexure B of the Circular.

  • VFEX TRANSACTION (RESOLUTIONS 5 TO 8)

At the Meeting, Shareholders will be asked to ratify certain agreements and an issue of securities made in connection with the VFEX Transaction as announced on 9 November 2026, in connection with a capital raising in Zimbabwe of a minimum of US$3,000,000 and a maximum of US$5,000,000 and the Secondary Listing on the VFEX.

  • XINHAI INVESTMENT AGREEMENT (RESOLUTIONS 9 AND 10)

At the Meeting, Shareholders will be asked to ratify the issue of the Tranche 3 CDIs and options in accordance with Investment Agreement between the Company and Xinhai as announced on 19 December 2025, under which Xinhai agreed to make a total investment worth up to A$11,000,000 in the Company in exchange for up to 36,666,667 CDIs at an issue price of A$0.30 per CDI, in three tranches.

  • SHARE AUTHORITIES TO BE PROPOSED UNDER RESOLUTIONS 11 AND 12

Section 561 of the 2006 Act provides that subject to limited exceptions any shares being issued must be offered to all existing shareholders pro-rata to their holding. However, where Directors have a general authority to allot shares, they may be given the power by the Company’s articles of association or by a special resolution to allot shares pursuant to the authority as if the statutory pre-emption rights did not exist. Resolution 11 will be proposed as an ordinary resolution for additional Directors’ general authority, pursuant to section 551 of the 2006 Act, to issue equity securities up to an aggregate nominal amount of £1,000,000.

Resolution 12 will be proposed as a special resolution for additional Directors' authority to allot equity securities for cash without first offering them to the shareholders pro-rata to their holdings, pursuant to section 570 of the 2006 Act up to an aggregate nominal amount of £500,000.

The authorities mentioned above will, if passed, expire at the conclusion of the next Annual General Meeting or the date being 15 months from the passing of the resolutions, whichever is the earlier and will be in addition to existing authorities, and any authorities granted pursuant to any other Resolutions proposed at the General Meeting and as set out in the Notice of General Meeting.

The Directors have no current intention to utilise these additional authorities but wish to give the Company flexibility in the event that an opportunity arises to raise funds by way of an issue of equity securities.

RECOMMENDATION

The Directors consider that each of the Resolutions is in the best interests of the Company and its Shareholders as a whole. Accordingly, the Directors unanimously recommend that Shareholders vote in favour of Resolutions 1 and 5 to 12.

Dr Kerim Sener, Andrew du Toit and Michael Atkins each have a personal interest in the Resolution concerning the grant of an award to him (Resolutions 2, 3 and 4 respectively). Each of them did not participate in the Board’s consideration of that Resolution and makes no recommendation to Shareholders in respect of it.

The Directors other than Dr Sener recommend that Shareholders vote in favour of Resolution 2 (as they intend to do), the Directors other than Mr du Toit recommend that Shareholders vote in favour of Resolution 3 (as they intend to do), and the Directors other than Mr Atkins recommend that Shareholders vote in favour of Resolution 4 (as they intend to do).

The Chair intends to vote all available undirected proxies in favour of each Resolution, other than Resolution 4 in respect of which he will pass the Chair position to Michael de Villiers (as Deputy Chair), who intends to vote all available undirected proxies in favour of Resolution 4.

The Notice of General Meeting is set out in the Company’s circular dated 27 November 2026 (“Circular”), which is set out in full in the Appendix to this announcement and which will be made available on the Company’s website: https://www.arianaresources.com/investors/circulars.

  • VFEX TRANSACTION (RESOLUTIONS 5 TO 8)

At the Meeting, Shareholders will be asked to ratify certain agreements and an issue of securities made in connection with the Transaction. Shareholders should read and consider the following information before voting.

Overview

As announced on 9 November 2026, the VFEX has approved the VFEX Prospectus in connection with a capital raising in Zimbabwe of a minimum of US$3,000,000 and a maximum of US$5,000,000 and the Secondary Listing.

The Transaction comprises three sequential steps:

  • First, Dendere has agreed to subscribe for new Ordinary Shares as cornerstone investor under the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement, and the Company has agreed to grant Dendere the Call Option under the Call Option Agreement (Resolutions 5 to 7);
  • Second, the Company is offering the Placement Shares to selected eligible institutional and qualifying retail investors in Zimbabwe under the Private Placement (Resolution 8); and
  • Third, following completion of the Private Placement, the Company will apply for the admission of its Ordinary Shares to the official list of the VFEX. The Secondary Listing does not itself involve the issue of any securities.

The subscription by Dendere and the Private Placement together constitute the Company's capital raising in Zimbabwe. The Ordinary Shares subscribed for by Dendere count towards the minimum and maximum raise, but are issued under the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement and not under the VFEX Prospectus.

All new Ordinary Shares will be issued on the Zimbabwe Register and will be admitted to trading on AIM but will not be quoted on ASX unless and until they are transferred to be held in the form of CDIs, in which case the Company will apply for quotation of those CDIs.

The Cornerstone Subscription Agreement, the Call Option Agreement and the Private Placement are not subject to Shareholder approval. The Company agreed to issue the Tranche 1 Shares and Tranche 2 Shares and to grant the Call Option, and will issue the Placement Shares, using its placement capacity under ASX Listing Rule 7.1. Resolutions 5 to 8 seek Shareholder ratification of those agreements and that issue for the purposes of ASX Listing Rule 7.4 so that the Company’s placement capacity is refreshed to the extent of the securities the subject of those Resolutions.

  • Cornerstone Subscription Agreement

The Company has entered into the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement with Dendere. Dendere acts on behalf of its investing partners.

The Cornerstone Subscription Agreement provides for Dendere to subscribe for Ordinary Shares in up to two tranches, as follows:

  • Tranche 1: Dendere has agreed, on a firm basis, to subscribe for the 45,454,545 Tranche 1 Shares at the Cornerstone Price for an aggregate subscription amount of US$1,000,000; and
  • Tranche 2: the Company may, in its sole discretion, by notice given to Dendere after the Private Placement closes and no later than 10 business days after that date, offer Dendere the opportunity to subscribe for up to 45,454,545 Tranche 2 Shares at the Cornerstone Price for up to a further US$1,000,000.

A summary of the material terms of the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement is set out in Annexure C. Further information is also contained in the Company’s ASX announcement dated 9 November 2026.

  • Call Option Agreement

The Company has entered into the Call Option Agreement with Dendere, under which, with effect from, and conditional on, completion of the subscription for the Tranche 1 Shares, the Company will grant Dendere the Call Option at an exercise price of US$0.035 per Option Share, payable in cash in US dollars on exercise. The Call Option is to be granted in consideration of Dendere's obligations under the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement and no premium is payable for it. The Call Option will be exercisable from the date of the Secondary Listing and will expire 12 months after completion of the subscription for the Tranche 1 Shares.

The number of Option Shares is the subscription monies paid by Dendere under the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement divided by the exercise price, rounded down to the nearest whole Ordinary Share. On the amounts in the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement, the Call Option will be over:

  • 28,571,428 Option Shares, if only the Tranche 1 Shares are issued;
  • 57,142,857 Option Shares, if the Tranche 2 Shares are issued in full; or
  • a proportionate number of Option Shares between those two figures, if the Tranche 2 Shares are issued in part.

The maximum number of Option Shares is 57,142,857. If the Tranche 2 Shares are not issued in full, the Call Option over the excess lapses automatically without compensation. A summary of the material terms of the Call Option Agreement is set out in Annexure D.

  • Private Placement

The capital raising in Zimbabwe comprises the issue of up to 221,343,874 new Ordinary Shares, raising a minimum of US$3.0 million and a maximum of US$5.0 million in aggregate, comprising:

  • up to 90,909,090 Ordinary Shares to be subscribed for by Dendere at the Cornerstone Price of US$0.022 per Ordinary Share under Tranche 1 and, if taken up, Tranche 2 of the Cornerstone Subscription Agreement; and

Use of Funds

The gross proceeds of the capital raising will first be applied to the estimated expenses of the capital raising and the Secondary Listing (approximately US$110,244). The net proceeds will be applied to the two-year exploration and project development programme for the Dokwe Project formulated by the Competent Person for the Independent Geologist Report, including resource extension drilling, target generation, exploration and sterilisation drilling and project generation elsewhere in Zimbabwe. The general working capital and corporate overheads of the Group will be met from the Group’s existing cash resources and not from the proceeds of the capital raising.

ASX Listing Rule 7.1

Broadly speaking, and subject to a number of exceptions, ASX Listing Rule 7.1 limits the amount of equity securities that a listed company can issue without the approval of its shareholders over any 12 month period to 15% of the fully paid ordinary shares it had on issue at the start of that period.

ASX Listing Rule 7.2 (Exception 13)

ASX Listing Rule 7.2 (Exception 13(b)) provides that ASX Listing Rule 7.1 does not apply to an issue of securities under an employee incentive scheme if, within three years before the date of issue of the securities, the holders of the entity’s ordinary securities have approved the issue of equity securities under the scheme as an exception to ASX Listing Rule 7.1.

Exception 13(b) is only available if and to the extent that the number of equity securities issued under the scheme does not exceed the maximum number set out in the entity’s notice of meeting dispatched to shareholders in respect of the meeting at which shareholder approval was obtained pursuant to ASX Listing Rule 7.2 (Exception 13(b)). Exception 13(b) also ceases to be available if there is a material change to the terms of the scheme from those set out in the notice of meeting.

ANNEXURE A – Summary of LTIP

This Annexure forms part of the Explanatory Statement accompanying the Notice of General Meeting.

Introduction

The LTIP is a discretionary share plan which gives participants the right to acquire Ordinary Shares subject to the satisfaction of performance conditions and, normally, continued service. Its purpose is to incentivise and retain the executive directors, senior management and other key contributors of the Group, and to align their interests with those of Shareholders. The LTIP will be administered by the Company’s remuneration committee (“Committee”). In this summary, references to Ordinary Shares include CDIs representing Ordinary Shares where the context permits.

Eligibility

Any employee of the Group (including executive directors) may be selected to participate in the LTIP. Individuals who are not employees but provide substantial services to the Group, such as non-executive directors, consultants and contractors, may participate under a non-employee sub-plan. The Committee will decide who participates and the number of Ordinary Shares over which awards are granted. While the Company is listed on ASX, awards to directors (and their associates and other persons within ASX Listing Rule 10.14) require prior Shareholder approval under ASX Listing Rule 10.14, unless an exception applies.

Operation

Awards may be granted as conditional rights to receive Ordinary Shares automatically on vesting (“Allocations”) or as options to acquire Ordinary Shares at an exercise price set by the Committee, which may be nil (“Options”). Awards to participants in Australia will normally be granted as performance rights, being nil-cost options which are exercised by notice once vested (“Performance Rights”). No payment is required for the grant of an award, although arrangements must be made to fund the nominal value of any newly issued Ordinary Shares where required by law.

Awards will normally only be granted within 42 days after the announcement of the Company’s results for any period or the date of any general meeting, or at other times where the Committee considers that circumstances justify a grant, in each case subject to any dealing restrictions. Awards may not be granted after the tenth anniversary of the adoption of the LTIP.

Individual limits

The aggregate market value of Ordinary Shares subject to awards granted to a participant in respect of any financial year may not normally exceed 100% of salary (or fixed fees, for non-employees), or 150% in exceptional circumstances. Where an award relates to more than one financial year, its value may be spread across those years when applying this limit. The initial awards to be granted in 2026 (“2026 Awards”) will represent each participant’s aggregate long-term incentive opportunity for the three financial years beginning on 1 July 2026. The number of Ordinary Shares under each 2026 Award has been calculated using a reference price of 2 pence per Ordinary Share and will not be recalculated on vesting or exercise.

Satisfying awards and dilution limits

Awards may be satisfied by the issue of new Ordinary Shares (or CDIs), the transfer of treasury shares or the transfer of existing Ordinary Shares, and the Committee may also settle awards in cash. The number of Ordinary Shares which may be issued (or transferred from treasury) to satisfy awards granted in any ten-year period under the LTIP and any other employees’ share scheme adopted by the Company may not exceed 10% of the Company’s issued ordinary share capital from time to time. Awards that have lapsed or been released, or which are to be satisfied in cash or with existing Ordinary Shares (other than treasury shares), do not count towards this limit. Treasury shares will count for so long as institutional investor guidelines require. Separately, the number of equity securities issued in reliance on ASX Listing Rule 7.2, Exception 13(b) may not exceed the maximum set out under “ASX Listing Rules” below.

Vesting and exercise

An award (or part of an award) will normally vest when the Committee has determined the extent to which the applicable performance condition has been satisfied and the Company has notified the participant. Different parts of an award may vest at different times. Allocations will be settled within 30 days of vesting. Options may be exercised from vesting until the expiry date set at grant (31 December 2030 for the 2026 Awards), which may be no later than the tenth anniversary of grant. Any part of an award which has not vested (or, in the case of an Option, been exercised) by its expiry date will lapse. The Committee may settle an award in cash or settle an Option by delivering Ordinary Shares equal in value to the gain on exercise. Where awards are settled in CDIs, the number delivered will reflect the CDI ratio at settlement (currently one CDI for every ten Ordinary Shares). If a dealing restriction prevents a participant from exercising a vested Option immediately before the end of its exercise period, the exercise period will be extended until 20 dealing days after the restriction ceases to apply (unless the restriction arose from the participant’s misconduct), even if this is after the expiry date. The Committee may also delay vesting, exercise or settlement to the extent reasonably necessary to comply with applicable law or a dealing restriction, obtain a required consent or approval, satisfy tax, or complete an investigation relevant to malus or clawback. Under the Zimbabwe addendum, a vested Option may be exercised only at a time and in a manner notified by the Committee (which may include automatic exercise and the sale of some or all of the resulting Ordinary Shares), and exercise and settlement may be delayed to comply with exchange control and other legal requirements. Any such delay will not extend the period during which the Option may be exercised, which will end on its expiry date (subject to the dealing restriction extension described above).

Dividend equivalents

The Committee may decide that participants will receive an amount (in cash and/or Ordinary Shares) equal in value to the dividends that would have been paid on their vested Ordinary Shares between grant and vesting. The 2026 Awards do not carry this right.

Holding periods

The Committee may require vested Ordinary Shares (net of any tax) to be held for a post-vesting holding period, normally ending on the second anniversary of vesting, during which they may not be sold except to fund tax. A holding period will end early on a takeover or the participant’s death. No holding period will apply to the 2026 Awards.

Performance conditions

Awards may be granted subject to one or more performance conditions linked to the performance of the Company, the Group and/or the participant, which will determine the proportion (if any) of an award that vests. Performance conditions must normally be set on or before grant. The Committee may amend or substitute a performance condition in accordance with its terms, or if an event occurs which makes this appropriate, provided that the amended condition is not materially less challenging and continues to achieve its original purpose. A performance condition may be waived only where its terms expressly permit. The Committee may also amend or waive any other condition applying to an award if it reasonably considers that an event has occurred which makes this appropriate, provided that the amendment or waiver does not materially increase the value of the award.

The 2026 Awards will be subject to performance conditions measured from 1 July 2026, reflecting the three financial years to which the awards relate. Each 2026 Award is divided into two equal tranches, each of which is divided into sub-tranches. Each sub-tranche is assessed separately and may vest at a different time before the awards expire on 31 December 2030:

•          Share Price Tranche (50% of each award): this tranche rewards sustained share price growth. It is divided into three sub-tranches, weighted 25%, 25% and 50% of the tranche and measured on 30 June 2027, 30 June 2028 and 30 June 2029 respectively, so that greater weight is placed on longer-term performance. Performance is measured using the volume-weighted average price of an Ordinary Share on AIM over the 15 consecutive dealing days ending on the relevant measurement date, which reduces the effect of short-term price movements. The threshold and target prices are 2.7 pence and 3.0 pence for the first sub-tranche, 3.6 pence and 4.0 pence for the second sub-tranche, and 4.5 pence and 5.0 pence for the third sub-tranche. Nothing will vest below the threshold price; 50% of the sub-tranche will vest at the threshold price; and vesting will increase on a straight-line basis to 100% at or above the target price. Each sub-tranche is assessed once only, by reference to its own measurement date, and there is no retesting. However, if the average price, measured on the same basis, equals or exceeds the target price for a sub-tranche at any time before its measurement date, that sub-tranche will be treated as satisfied in full at that point.

•          Dokwe Milestone Tranche (50% of each award): this tranche rewards delivery of the Company’s Dokwe gold project in Zimbabwe. It is divided into a construction sub-tranche (25% of the tranche) and a commercial production sub-tranche (75% of the tranche). The construction milestone is achieved when all of the following have occurred: a final investment decision by the board of the Company (or the relevant Group company) approving the project’s development plan; legally binding project funding sufficient to construct and commission the project, with all material conditions to initial availability satisfied or waived; the material permits required to begin construction; and the commencement of material permanent construction works and mobilisation of the principal construction contractor (preparatory works do not count). The construction sub-tranche will vest in full if the construction milestone is achieved on or before 31 March 2028 and as to 50% if it is achieved after that date but on or before 30 June 2028 and will otherwise lapse. Commercial production is achieved when the project has completed commissioning and operated for a continuous period of 30 days at an average rate of at least 80% of the processing capacity specified in its approved development plan, in each case evidenced to the Committee’s reasonable satisfaction. The commercial production sub-tranche will vest in full if commercial production commences on or before 30 June 2029 and as to 50% if it commences after that date but on or before 31 December 2029 and will otherwise lapse. Each sub-tranche may vest only once.

The Committee will determine the extent to which each sub-tranche vests as soon as reasonably practicable after the relevant measurement date, milestone or longstop date, and may rely on such calculations, evidence and independent advice as it considers appropriate. The number of Ordinary Shares vesting under each tranche is calculated separately.

Before an award vests, the Committee may reduce (but not increase) the number of Ordinary Shares that would otherwise vest if it considers that the outcome produced by the performance conditions would be manifestly unjustified or anomalous, having regard to the overall performance of the Company and any other relevant circumstances.

Malus and clawback

This period may be extended while an investigation is ongoing. The relevant events include a material misstatement of financial results or other performance measures, a material error in determining the grant or vesting of an award, fraud or serious misconduct by the participant, a material breach of restrictive covenants, conduct causing material financial loss or reputational damage, a material failure of risk management or a material safety or environmental incident, and corporate failure. Any other circumstances

HSNG is a leading Nordic sports nutrition and supplements group, combining well-established e-commerce platforms such as Gymgrossisten, Bodystore and Proteinfabrikken with strong own product brands, including Star Nutrition and Vitaprana. We would like to thank all HSNG employees for a great partnership over many years, and wish them all the best going forward,” says Nils K. Selte, President and CEO of Orkla.

The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals from the Swedish authorities, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027.

data.title: Gold demand revives in India, China as price slide sparks bargain buying
data.description:
Key points:
  • International spot gold prices hit lowest level since August 2025 this week
  • Gold traded at $9/oz premium in China this week
  • Indian dealers quote up to $19/oz premium this week
  • Indian jewellers replenishing stocks-dealer

By Sukanya Mitra and Rajendra Jadhav

Gold demand in top Asian hubs improved this week after prices fell to their lowest level in more than a year, drawing bargain-hunting jewellery and investment buyers to the market in India, while robust retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

International spot gold prices fell to their lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday after hot US inflation data cemented expectations of interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

In India, domestic gold prices (MAUc1) were trading around 124,800 rupees per 10 grams on Friday, after falling to 117,906 rupees earlier this week, the lowest level since October 28, 2025.

“Buyers were not expecting such a sharp price correction. The decline is now driving a pickup in jewellery purchases among retail consumers, while also boosting demand for coins and bars from investors,” said Chirag ​Thakkar, chief executive of bullion dealer Amrapali Group Gujarat.

Dealers quoted premium (XAU-IN-PREM) of up to $19 an ounce over official domestic prices this week, inclusive of 15% import and 3% sales levies, compared to the last week’s premium of up to $17.

Jewellers are replenishing stocks as the price correction has raised expectations of stronger demand during the wedding season, said a Mumbai-based bullion dealer with a private bank.

In China, bullion (XAU-CN-PREM) traded at $9-an-ounce premium over global benchmark prices.

"Dealers reported robust sales, with some shops running low on inventory, helping keep local premiums firm," said Peter Fung, head of dealing at Wing Fung Precious Metals.

Meanwhile, China's net gold imports via Hong Kong in October rose 1.6% from the previous month, hitting their highest level since April, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Thursday.

In Singapore (XAU-SG-PREM), gold traded between a $0.5 discount and a $1.80 premium this week, while in Hong Kong (XAU-HK-PREM), gold was sold at a $2 premium.

Elsewhere, in Japan (XAU-TK-PREM), gold traded in a range from a $0.5 discount to a $0.5 premium this week.
